adversarial_probes.a_tenant_smuggling: GET /api/rights/tenant-state with a real second tenant (tenant-b, freshly seeded via direct SQL with its own owner e-tenantb-owner holding exactly 1 role) probed with 5 independent smuggling vectors: (1) ?tenant_id=<tenant-A-uuid> query param, (2) X-Tenant-Id: <tenant-A-uuid> header, (3) Cookie: tenant_id=<tenant-A-uuid>; active_tenant=<tenant-A-uuid>, (4) X-Active-Tenant-Id / X-Choros-Tenant headers, (5) same-tenant employee_id query-param smuggling (ordinary actor e-mironov with ?employee_id=<other-employee-uuid>). ALL FIVE returned the response scoped strictly to the AUTHENTICATED caller's own tenant/identity — tenant-b's owner never saw tenant A's 9 roles under any vector; e-mironov's response never changed based on the employee_id query param. Additional fake-admin-header probe (x-admin/x-can-manage/x-role/x-is-owner on an ordinary actor) also had zero effect on can_manage. A duplicate/conflicting x-dev-user header (curl merges into a single comma-joined value) correctly failed closed with 403 ACTOR_TENANT_UNRESOLVED rather than resolving to either identity. Root cause confirmed by code read: resolveActorTenant/resolveCallerEmployeeId (src/http/rights-overview.ts) take ONLY the auth-resolved actorId as input — there is structurally no tenant/employee parameter on this endpoint to spoof, matching the ADR/spec claim verbatim.
adversarial_probes.b_semi_confirmed_invisibility: Planted a critical grant via the REAL write API (not SQL): POST /api/grants {role_id: budget-approver, resource_type: record, operation: approve, scope:{kind:tags,tags:[]}} as e-owner → server responded {state:'semi-confirmed', second_approver_required:true, reason:'escalates_criticality'}. Immediately re-read GET /api/rights/tenant-state as BOTH e-owner (admin projection) and e-mironov (self projection, the role holder) — in both, role.grants (active) was empty of the new grant id, role.pending.grants contained it with confirmed_by:'e-owner'. Then completed the cycle via the EXISTING second-confirm path: POST /api/grants {phase:'confirm2', change_ref:<grantId>} as e-larina (a genuinely distinct third employee) → {state:'confirmed'}; both projections immediately showed the grant in active .grants and pending.grants was empty. Grant then revoked via POST /api/grants/:id/revoke to leave the test DB clean (torn down entirely afterward anyway). This proves AC-8's 'never in any active projection' claim against a REAL escalating write, not just a seeded DB row.
adversarial_probes.c_ordinary_employee_self_view: Live GET /api/rights/tenant-state as e-mironov (ordinary employee, holds only budget-approver, no mgmt_object grant) returned scope:'self', can_manage:false, and EXACTLY 1 role (budget-approver, with only mironov's own assignment). Cross-checked against the admin (e-owner) full view of the same tenant (9 roles total, including role-approver→e-larina, role-initiator→e-orlov, role-configurator→e-configurator/assistant-agent, tenant-owner→e-owner) — none of those other employees' assignments/roles leaked into mironov's self-projection. can_manage:true was never obtainable via header spoofing (see probe a).
